qiete.mean: making no noise, calm and still
qiete.ex: The class became quiet when the teacher entered.

qualified.ex: She is highly qualified for this teaching post.
qualified.mn: qualified – quality wala banda, job ke liye fit

quarrelsome.ex: His quarrelsome nature annoyed his neighbours.
quarrelsome.mn: quarrelsome – quarrel karne wala jhagdalu insaan

queit.mean: spelling mistake of quiet; means no noise
queit.ex: The class was queit when the teacher entered.

questionaire.mean: wrong spelling of questionnaire (a form with questions)
questionaire.ex: The teacher said the questionaire has ten questions.

quicken.ex: She quickened her pace to catch the bus.

quintessential.mean: most perfect example of a quality
quintessential.ex: He is the quintessential English gentleman.
quintessential.mn: quintessential – fifth essence, sabse perfect example

quorum.mean: minimum members needed for valid meeting
quorum.ex: The meeting was cancelled for lack of a quorum.
quorum.mn: quorum – meeting valid hone ka minimum count

quack.mean: cry of a duck; a fake doctor
quack.ex: That quack sold useless herbal cures to sick villagers.
quack.mn: quack – nakli doctor jo duck jaisa 'quack' bolke ilaaj karta hai

qualify.ex: She had to qualify before joining the national team.
qualify.mn: qualify – quality dikhao tabhi eligible bano

quarter.ex: He ate a quarter of the pizza.
quarter.mn: quarter – char hisse mein se ek quarter

quell.mean: suppress or put an end to
quell.ex: Troops were sent to quell the riot.
quell.mn: quell – 'kill' jaisa lagta hai, police ne danga kill/dabaa diya

questionnaire.mean: set of printed questions for survey
questionnaire.ex: Please fill out this questionnaire before the interview.
questionnaire.mn: questionnaire – question ka naala, ek ke baad ek sawaal

quientessential.mean: wrong spelling of quintessential (the best example)

quotient.mean: result of dividing one number by another
quotient.ex: Divide sixty by five to get the quotient.
quotient.mn: quotient – 'quotation' nahi, bhaag ka answer, IQ ka Q

quarrelled.mean: had an angry argument or dispute
quarrelled.ex: They quarrelled over money all night.
quarrelled.mn: quarrel-led – quarrel yaani ladai ki gayi

quadrangle.mean: four-sided courtyard enclosed by buildings; a quadrilateral
quadrangle.ex: Students gathered in the college quadrangle after class.
quadrangle.mn: quadrangle – quad (chaar) angle wala aangan, college ka square courtyard

quality.mean: standard or degree of excellence of something
quality.ex: The quality of this fabric is excellent.
quality.mn: quality – 'kis quality ka maal hai?' matlab kaisa achha hai

quasi.mean: seemingly, resembling but not truly so
quasi.ex: He held a quasi-official position without real power.
quasi.mn: quasi – 'kya-si' cheez, dikhti waisi par asli nahi

quench.ex: She drank water to quench her thirst.
quench.mn: quench – 'kaunch' ke paani se pyaas bujhao

questions.mean: sentences asking for information; matters to resolve
questions.ex: The teacher answered all the students' questions.
questions.mn: questions – quest (khoj) me answer dhundo, sawal

quiescent.ex: The volcano remained quiescent for centuries.
quiescent.mn: quiescent – 'quiet-scent', shaant aur nishkriya pada hua

quinton.mean: a boy's name, also an old string instrument
quinton.bn: একটি ছেলের নাম বা পুরোনো বাদ্যযন্ত্র
quinton.ex: Quinton scored the highest marks in the class test.

queen.ex: The queen addressed the nation on television.
queen.mn: queen – rani, raja ki patni ya shaasak

quadruped.mn: quad bike ke chaar pahiye, quadruped ke chaar pair

quandary.ex: She was in a quandary about which job to accept.
quandary.mn: quandary – kaun sa raasta? confusion mein phasa banda

quavering.ex: He answered in a quavering voice.
quavering.mn: quavering – ghabra kar aawaz kaanpne lagi

quenched.ex: She quenched her thirst with cold water.
quenched.mn: quenched – thanda paani se pyaas bujh gayi

queue.ex: We stood in a long queue for tickets.
queue.mn: queue – Q ke peeche log line mein khade

quiet.mn: quiet – kya-yet? chup raho, koi awaaz nahi

quirky.ex: He has a quirky sense of humour.
quirky.mn: quirky – thoda alag, ajeeb sa banda

quaint.ex: They stayed in a quaint little cottage by the sea.
quaint.mn: quaint – purane zamane ka pyaara sa gaon, cute aur alag

quarantine.ex: Travelers were placed in quarantine for two weeks.
quarantine.mn: quarantine – 40 (quarant) din tak alag rakho bimari se

quay.mean: a landing place for ships; wharf
quay.ex: The boat was tied up at the quay.
quay.mn: quay – 'key' bola jaata, jahaaz ke ghat pe khada

query.ex: I sent a query to the support team.
query.mn: query – computer mein search ka sawaal, quer=poochna

quever.mean: not a real word, likely typo of quaver
quever.bn: সঠিক শব্দ নয়, quaver-এর ভুল বানান
quever.ex: The teacher said 'quever' is not a proper word.

quiete.mean: not a real English word, typo of quiet
quiete.ex: 'Quiete' is not a proper English word.

quit.mean: to leave or stop doing something
quit.ex: She decided to quit her job.
quit.mn: quit – job chhod do, free ho jao

questionable.mean: doubtful; of uncertain honesty or value
questionable.ex: His questionable methods raised eyebrows among colleagues.
questionable.mn: questionable – jiske upar question uthe, doubtful cheez

quake.mean: to shake or tremble, often from fear
quake.ex: The ground began to quake during the earthquake.
quake.mn: quake – earthquake mein zameen kaanpti hai

quarrel.ex: They had a quarrel over money.
quarrel.mn: quarrel – 'kar-rail' do log rail pe ladte hue

queer.ex: He had a queer feeling about the house.

quintesential.ex: 'Quintesential' is a spelling mistake, please correct it.

quiver.mean: to shake with a slight rapid motion
quiver.ex: Her lips began to quiver with emotion.

qualities.ex: Honesty is one of her best qualities.
qualities.mn: qualities – kaunsi quali (kaisi) hai, uske gun.

queer pitch.mean: a strange or unfair situation to deal with
queer pitch.ex: The new rules made a queer pitch for the cricket team.

queer somebody's pitch.mean: to spoil someone's plan or chance
queer somebody's pitch.ex: Rahul's idea queered Priya's pitch for the school competition.

quick sell out.bn: খুব তাড়াতাড়ি সব বিক্রি হয়ে যাওয়া
quick sell out.ex: The cricket bat was a quick sell out at the shop.

quickly and expectedly.mean: in a fast way that we already knew would happen
quickly and expectedly.ex: Rahul finished the exam quickly and expectedly, as usual.

quickly and unexpectedly.mean: in a fast way that surprised everyone
quickly and unexpectedly.ex: Mona's team won the match quickly and unexpectedly.

quite.ex: The exam was quite hard for Sita.

quite ordinary.ex: Her lunch was quite ordinary, just dal and rice.
